elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “Client and its affiliates.”

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant expressly covers “contractors acting on Client's behalf.”

Although the added sentence says fully paid licences are perpetual, §c still states that “the license shall last until this Agreement is terminated.” No notwithstanding language or conforming amendment resolves this conflicting duration.

The added sentence calls paid-up licences irrevocable, but §c continues to end the licence when the Agreement terminates, including potentially through TrueLink's termination rights. The operative provisions do not unambiguously preserve the licence against revocation through agreement termination.

elements.element: Subscription licences are terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The new sentence restricts only termination “by TrueLink,” while §c still provides for the subscription licence to end whenever the Agreement is terminated under §12. Thus the licence may expire through other termination routes or triggers.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to successors.
elements.evidence: The assignment carve-out is limited to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets, rather than successors generally.

elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates upon written notice.
elements.evidence: The licence extends to Client's affiliates unconditionally, which is broader than coverage requiring written notice.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: Section 15 permits assignment without approval “to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets,” covering the specified M&A succession circumstances.

result.reason: The redline satisfies the fallback through unconditional affiliate coverage and an M&A-successor assignment carve-out. It does not satisfy the preferred position because successor transferability is transaction-limited and §c's surviving agreement-linked licence term conflicts with the added paid-up and subscription protections. It is not minimal to the completed fallback because it also adds contractors and attempted paid-up/subscription protections, yet does not complete the preferred position. The unresolved term conflict also prevents a finding that the drafting preserves intent without contradiction.
